item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Best Lovable prompts to build an app faster (8 to copy)","dek":"Eight copy and paste prompts built on Lovable's own docs, for planning, design, login, scoped changes and bug fixes that do not waste credits.","summary":"Eight Lovable prompts based on Lovable's prompting best practices, prompt library and debugging guide. Each one asks for one change, names where it goes and says what must stay the same.","seo_title":"Best Lovable prompts: 8 to copy for building apps faster","seo_description":"8 Lovable prompts to copy: make it ask questions first, pick a design, add login, lock what must not change, report bugs and turn fixes into project rules.","answer_summary":"Good Lovable prompts ask for one change at a time, name the page or component, describe the result you want and say what must not change. For big changes, use Plan mode or ask Lovable to ask you questions before it builds.","tags":["Lovable","Prompts","Vibe coding","AI app builder","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The best Lovable prompts are short, scoped and specific. They say what to build, where it goes and what must stay the same. This guide collects eight prompts built on Lovable's own documentation: its prompting best practices, its prompt library and its debugging guide. Fill in the [brackets], send one prompt at a time and check the result before the next one.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Why this matters: every build costs credits, and Lovable fills any gap in your prompt with its own guesses. LowCode Agency founder Jesus Vargas, in a prompting guide updated on October 16, 2026, says those guesses are often wrong. His fix is four parts in every prompt: the current state of the project, the exact page or component, the result the user should see, and what must not change.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you are new to Lovable, start with our guide on how to use Lovable to build an app without coding. This one assumes you already have a project open.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Best Lovable prompts for planning","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Make Lovable ask you questions first","text":"I want to add [feature] to my app. Before you build anything, ask me any questions you need to fully understand what I want from this feature.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting best practices recommend closing a prompt with a request for clarifying questions, and say this works especially well in Plan mode. The prompt library gives the same advice for large prompts: ask Lovable to check its questions first, or use Plan mode to agree on the approach before it builds.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Have Lovable rewrite your prompt","text":"Here is a prompt I plan to send you: [paste your prompt]. Rewrite it to be clearer and more specific: name the pages, the components and what must not change. Do not build anything yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting handbook calls this meta prompting: you ask the AI to refine your prompt before you use it. The same handbook recommends scoped edits, where you tell the AI to change only certain files or sections and leave other pages alone.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A rewrite costs one message and often saves several. A vague prompt like \"make the dashboard better\" can turn into a long chain of fixes, while a rewritten version names the cards, the chart and the table you actually want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Three design directions before building","text":"Describe three different design directions for the hero section of [your app] before you build anything. For each one, give the style, the colors and the fonts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library includes a prompt that asks for three directions for the hero section before anything is built, plus ready-made style prompts for minimal, glassmorphic, bold, playful, calm and editorial looks. Its best practices page suggests picking the style early and saving your chosen keywords in the project's instructions so every later prompt uses them.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for building features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Add login the right way","text":"Add sign up, log in and forgot password pages that match the app's current style. Require login before the dashboard. Add a Sign in with Google button next to email and password. Show clear error and success states on every form.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is based on the sign up and login prompt in Lovable's prompt library, which runs on Lovable's built-in backend. The library says each of its prompts is meant to work as a single Build mode message, and that some features need a paid plan: payments need Pro or higher, and email alerts need a paid plan.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use real words, not placeholder text. Lovable's best practices say real headlines and button labels show layout problems early, and that you should plan for logged-in and logged-out states and for empty, loading and error states.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Lock what must not change","text":"Only change the [page or component]. [The change you want]. Do not touch the login flow, the payment code or any other page. When you are done, tell me which files you changed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's best practices tell you to set boundaries: what to build, where it goes and what must stay unchanged, with \"only change the orders page\" as an example. Its debugging guide adds that guardrails for fragile areas such as authentication or payments belong in the same prompt as the task.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for fixing bugs","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Report a bug Lovable can fix","text":"On the [page name] page, [what is broken]. I expected [what should happen], but instead [what happens]. Here is the exact error: [paste error]. This worked before [your last change]. What is the root cause? Explain it in simple terms before you change any code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's debugging guide describes a bug in four parts: what is broken, where it happens, what you expected and what happened instead. Add a screenshot for layout problems and the exact error text. Lovable reads console logs from the preview on its own, but errors on the published site have to be pasted in.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The guide says to use the Try to fix button once or twice when an error appears. Accounts get 10 free fixes, and each one comes back 24 hours after it is used. If the same error keeps returning, switch to Plan mode and find the root cause first, because repeated blind fixes tend to hide the real problem.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Test the whole flow in the browser","text":"Use browser testing to check that [the flow, for example sign up to checkout] works from start to finish. If something fails, reproduce it, fix it and test it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library has prompts that ask it to use browser testing to check a flow such as checkout, and to reproduce a bug in the browser, fix it and then confirm the fix. It also includes a security review prompt that checks the login flow and whether API routes are secure.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Turn the fix into a project rule","text":"We just fixed [the bug]. Summarize what went wrong, what we tried and the fix that worked, as a short rule I can add to the project instructions so this does not happen again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's handbook calls this reverse meta prompting, and its debugging guide gives the same advice: after a hard bug, ask Lovable to summarize the problem and the fix so it can go into project instructions. Instructions, previously called Knowledge, are read with every message. You set them in Project settings, then Instructions, with a limit of 10,000 characters.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Instructions (Knowledge)","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/features/knowledge"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What these prompts cannot fix","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Good prompts do not remove every limit. Vargas writes that if three targeted corrections fail on the same issue, the cause may be a limit of the platform rather than the prompt. Lovable's own debugging guide suggests restoring a working state from version history, or editing an earlier message and choosing Revert and resend, then telling Lovable what you did.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The pattern behind all eight prompts is the same: one change per message, a clear place, a clear result and a clear limit. Plan first when the change is big, and write down what worked so the next prompt starts from it. That is slower for the first ten minutes and faster for the rest of the project.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use GPTZero (and how accurate AI detectors are)","dek":"How to run a GPTZero scan, read the AI probability and confidence score, check a Google Doc's writing history, and what independent tests say about accuracy.","summary":"GPTZero scans pasted text or uploaded files and says whether it looks AI written, human written or mixed, with a probability and a confidence level. The free plan covers 10,000 words a month, and GPTZero itself says a result should not be the only proof of AI use.","seo_title":"How to use GPTZero and read its AI detection score","seo_description":"How to use GPTZero: paste or upload text, press Scan, read the AI probability and confidence level, check sentence highlights and know its accuracy limits.","answer_summary":"Go to gptzero.me, paste your text or upload a file and press Scan. Read the result as a probability that the whole text is AI, human or mixed, check the confidence level, and treat it as a starting point, not proof.","tags":["GPTZero","AI detector","AI writing","Education","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero is an AI detector: you give it text, and it tells you whether the text looks written by AI, by a human, or by both. If you want to know how to use GPTZero, the short version is: paste the text on gptzero.me, press Scan, then read both the percentage and the confidence line. The tool was built by Edward Tian, then a Princeton undergraduate, and launched in January 2023.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero","url":"https://gptzero.me/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: GPTZero","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The scan takes seconds. Reading the result correctly is the hard part, and it matters most when the result is about someone else's work. This guide covers both, plus what independent testers found about accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use GPTZero, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Paste your text or upload a file","text":"Open gptzero.me. The homepage has a text box with a limit of 10,000 characters; for longer scans, GPTZero says to create a free account first. Besides pasted text, GPTZero says it accepts DOCX, PDF and image files. The free plan allows up to 3 files in a batch upload.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Press Scan","text":"GPTZero's own instructions are short: paste raw text or upload your file and press Scan. The Basic AI Scan on the free plan returns an overall AI detection score for the document.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Read the label and the percentage","text":"Each result sorts the text into AI, human or mixed, and shows an AI probability. That percentage is not the share of the text that is AI. It is the model's probability for the whole document. GPTZero's example: a 4% AI result means that out of 100 similar cases, about 4 would be fully AI written, about 57 mixed and about 39 fully human.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the confidence level","text":"Under the score, GPTZero says how sure it is. Highly confident means an error rate under 2%, moderately confident means around 10%, and low confidence means 14% or higher. GPTZero says that when the model is unsure, it leans toward human with a low confidence score.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Look at the sentence highlights","text":"Advanced Scan shows which sentences and phrases affect the score most, ranked as high, medium or low impact. Sentences that are not highlighted can still affect the result, because the detector reads the text as a whole. The free plan includes one Advanced Scan to try it; the full feature is part of the Premium plan.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Scan longer passages when you can. GPTZero says its model performs best on longer texts and English prose, so a single paragraph gives a weaker signal than a full essay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Scan Google Docs with the browser extension","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's browser extension works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. GPTZero's Chrome page says it is free to install with a GPTZero account and comes with a monthly allowance of scans, highlighting sessions and chat messages, which paid plans raise. It can scan webpages when you ask it to, and in Google Docs it can scan automatically, color sentences by AI confidence and replay how the document was written.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Google Docs writing report","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/7001890416-what-is-the-google-docs-writing-report-for-origin"},{"name":"GPTZero: Chrome extension","url":"https://gptzero.me/chrome"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Watch a writing report","text":"Install the extension and log in. Open a Google Doc you can edit, then click Watch Writing Report in the GPTZero menu. The report replays the writing process and evaluates whether the typing pattern looks human. If you only have view access, the menu asks you to request edit access. The free plan has a usage limit on writing reports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you write your own work in Google Docs, the writing report is your best defense against a false flag: it shows the document being typed, edited and pasted over time, which a single score cannot.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free and paid plans include","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to GPTZero's support center, the free plan includes 10,000 words a month, up to 10,000 characters per scan, the Basic AI Scan and one Advanced Scan. Essential adds Grammar Check, AI Vocabulary Check and scans up to 50,000 characters. Premium adds the full Advanced Scan, Writing Feedback, Plagiarism Check and batches of up to 50 files. Professional adds LMS integration, scans up to 150,000 characters and batches of up to 250 files.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Free and paid plans","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/1272562776-what-is-the-difference-between-the-free-and-paid-for-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's support article does not list prices. PCWorld's review, published November 16, 2026, listed Premium at $23.99 a month, or $12.99 a month billed annually, with 300,000 words a month, and Professional at $45.99 a month, or $24.99 a month billed annually, with 500,000 words a month. PCWorld also noted that the free version may use your text for training.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How accurate GPTZero really is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero says it keeps its false positive rate, human text wrongly flagged as AI, at no more than 1%, and reports 96.5% accuracy on documents that mix human and AI writing. It says its false positive rate on essays by non-native English speakers from the TOEFL exam is 1.1%. These are the company's own benchmarks. GPTZero also states that no AI detector is 100% accurate and that a result should be a conversation starter, not the final verdict.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero: AI detection technology","url":"https://gptzero.me/technology"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"PCWorld ran 50 samples in five groups. GPTZero scored all 10 pure AI samples, from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, as 100% AI, and all 10 human samples as 0% AI. The weak spot was AI text edited by a person: one such sample scored 96% human and another 98% human. Results on human text lightly edited with AI were inconsistent.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Older research is less kind to detectors in general. A Stanford study led by James Zou tested seven detectors, GPTZero among them, on 91 TOEFL essays and found that on average they classified 61.22% as AI generated, while they were near perfect on essays by U.S. eighth graders. The researchers also showed that asking a chatbot to rewrite text in more literary language helped it evade detection. GPTZero says it has since trained on more ESL writing.","sources":[{"name":"Stanford HAI: AI detectors biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers"},{"name":"Liang et al.: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02819v3"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Early reporting raised the same worry. According to Wikipedia's summary, Futurism wrote in January 2023 that, based on the error rate it saw, teachers relying on the tool could falsely accuse nearly 20 percent of innocent students, and The Washington Post noted in August 2023 that even a small false positive rate could lead to wrongful accusations.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: GPTZero","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"GPTZero is good at the easy cases: raw chatbot output and plainly human writing. It is weaker when a person has reworked AI text, and every detector's error rate becomes a real person once you scan a whole class. Use it as a screening tool, read the confidence line, scan full documents, and back any concern with a writing report or a conversation before you decide anything.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist wants every AI lab to agree on a shared speed limit for smarter models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues most benchmarks are outdated, but perplexity, a score for how well a model predicts the next token, still tracks progress. Lower means better predictions. GPT-4 scored about 0.91 on OpenAI's measure. Below 0.8, the post says, models showed transformative skills in cybersecurity and math. Labs would agree not to cross a shared limit until monitoring catches up. Sam Altman called the post the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while. Sources: TechCrunch, Datastudios.

nf:hero.nf:alt: An OpenAI logo on a smartphone screen in front of lines of computer code.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"OpenAI chief scientist proposes industry limits on AI development tied to perplexity","dek":"Jakub Pachocki says a single prediction score could give AI labs a shared yardstick, and that they should agree not to pass a common threshold until monitoring improves.","summary":"OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a post on November 22, 2026 proposing that leading AI developers agree on common limits measured by perplexity. He wrote that OpenAI models with losses below 0.8 showed transformative capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics.","seo_title":"OpenAI's Pachocki proposes AI development limits tied to perplexity","seo_description":"OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes shared industry limits on AI progress measured by perplexity, with GPT-4 at about 0.91 and new skills below 0.8.","answer_summary":"Pachocki proposes that frontier AI labs use perplexity, a measure of how well a model predicts the next token, as a shared benchmark, and commit not to train past an agreed level until their ability to understand and monitor AI behavior reaches a concrete milestone.","tags":["OpenAI","Jakub Pachocki","AI safety","Perplexity","Sam Altman"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a post on November 22, 2026 titled Perplexity and Intelligence, in which he proposes that leading AI developers agree on common limits to how far they push their models. TechCrunch reported on the post that afternoon, and Datastudios published a detailed summary of its figures.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"},{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman praised the post on X, describing it as the most important thing the company had published in a while, according to TechCrunch.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why perplexity","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pachocki argues that benchmarks built around specific downstream tasks have gone out of date as models improved, while perplexity has stayed informative. Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average, and a lower score means better predictions. TechCrunch reported that the post includes a chart showing how the perplexity of OpenAI's models has fallen since GPT-3.5.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Datastudios, the figures are log-perplexity scores measured on a held-out dataset drawn from OpenAI's internal codebase. GPT-3.5 sat at roughly 0.99 and GPT-4 at roughly 0.91. Pachocki wrote that GPT-4 was able to use chain-of-thought reasoning productively at that level, and that once OpenAI's models reached losses below 0.8, the company saw transformative capabilities emerge in fields such as cybersecurity and mathematics.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"},{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios reported that the post also cites an unnamed OpenAI model at about 0.76, linked to strong results on open math problems, and expects further capability jumps somewhere around 0.68 to 0.7. The post does not say which model reached 0.76 or whether the lower range would serve as a limit.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the proposal asks of AI labs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pachocki suggests that perplexity could act as a shared benchmark for general intelligence, which companies could use to set common limits. Under the idea, developers would commit not to go past an agreed threshold until their ability to understand and monitor AI behavior reaches a concrete milestone, TechCrunch reported.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios described the plan in three layers: shared norms for evaluating and red-teaming frontier models before first use, along with transparency standards; commitments not to cross common limits defined by perplexity and other measures until a monitoring milestone is met, with a successor to chain-of-thought monitors given as an example; and a framework for setting later limits. The post names no partner companies and no date for a first limit, and it announces no change to ChatGPT, Codex or the API, according to Datastudios.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The post also lists open problems, Datastudios reported. Labs train on different datasets, perplexity does not map directly onto real tasks, gains from chain-of-thought reasoning do not lower perplexity, and nobody knows where the loss floor lies. OpenAI said it is publishing its own numbers as a first step, while acknowledging that this gives competitors a clearer view of its progress.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The wider push for limits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The proposal arrives as calls for restraint grow inside the industry. TechCrunch noted that Anthropic's IPO filing warned the technology could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society, and that Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has published a plan to pace the frontier, calling for common safety standards and limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress. Altman and Elon Musk reportedly endorsed that plan.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The notable part is less the idea of limits than the choice of a single number to define them. A shared metric would let rival labs check one another, but only if they agree on the dataset it is measured on, a problem the post itself raises. By publishing its own scores first, OpenAI is betting that openness will pull competitors into the same frame.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The test is whether Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI or Meta publish comparable perplexity figures or sign on to a common threshold. Without that, the proposal remains one company's yardstick.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to delete your Meta AI chats for good
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Meta AI app, tap Menu at the top left, then Settings at the bottom left. Under App settings, tap Data & privacy, then Manage your information. Confirm with Delete all. Your chats, prompts and media leave the History and Media sections. On meta.ai, click your profile picture, then Settings and the same path. Sources: Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes, Meta Help Center: Manage your information on Meta AI and Vibes, The Washington Post (via The Nightly): Your AI chatbot keeps a file on you, Meta Help Center: Meta AI and Vibes.

Public posts are removed separately with Remove all public vibes or Remove all public posts on the same screen.","tags":["Meta AI","Vibes","Privacy","Delete chats","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"How to delete Meta AI chats, in short: open Settings, go to Data & privacy, then Manage your information, and tap Delete all chats and media. That one screen exists in the Meta AI app, the Vibes app and on meta.ai in a browser, according to Meta's help center. It clears your history in one go. Anything you posted publicly needs a second button on the same screen.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/2457110494637611/"},{"name":"Meta Help Center: Manage your information on Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/1771195753735844/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This guide gives the exact taps for each version, then explains what deleting removes and what it leaves alone. Open Settings","text":"Tap Menu at the top left of the Meta AI app, then tap Settings at the bottom left.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Go to Manage your information","text":"Under App settings, tap Data & privacy, then tap Manage your information. This is the same screen where Meta lets you export a copy of your information, so grab an export first if you want to keep anything.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Delete everything","text":"Tap Delete all chats and media, then confirm with Delete all. Meta says your chats, prompts and media will no longer show in the History section or the Media section of the app.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The delete option on this screen clears everything at once, so export first if some of it is worth keeping.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"On the web at meta.ai","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. On a computer","text":"Go to www.meta.ai and click your profile picture at the bottom left. Click Settings, then Data & privacy, then Manage your information. Click Delete all chats and media, then Delete all. Meta says the chats, prompts and media then disappear from the History section and the Create section of the site.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. On a phone browser","text":"Go to www.meta.ai, tap the Menu icon, then tap your profile picture at the bottom left. Tap Settings, Data & privacy and Manage your information, then Delete all chats and media and Delete all. In the mobile browser, Meta calls the history area Recent instead of History.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"In the Vibes app","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Clear Vibes too","text":"Vibes keeps its own history. Tap Profile at the bottom right, then Settings at the top right, then Data & privacy and Manage your information. Tap Delete all chats and media, then Delete all.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Remove your public posts and vibes","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deleting your chats does not delete anything you made public, Meta's help center says. Public vibes and public posts are a separate step, and other people's vibes that include you stay visible unless you remove them under Media that includes me.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/2457110494637611/"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Remove all public vibes in the app","text":"On the same Manage your information screen in the Meta AI or Vibes app, tap Remove all public vibes, then Remove all.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Remove all public posts on the web","text":"On meta.ai, follow the same path and click Remove all public posts, then Remove all.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Remove just one","text":"To take down a single vibe in the Meta AI app, tap Menu, then your profile picture at the bottom right, open the vibe, tap the Menu icon and choose Remove from feed. In the Vibes app, start from Profile instead. On the web, open the post, click the Menu icon and choose Remove from feed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Removing a vibe from the feed does not erase it. Meta says removed vibes and posts stay in your Media or Create section, where you can post them again. Delete your chats and media as well if you want them gone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What deleting does not cover","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Voice chats behave a little differently. Meta says the recording of a voice conversation is only in your history temporarily, while the text transcript stays until you delete it. If you posted a prompt using your voice, the recording stays until you delete that post.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/2457110494637611/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Meta's help page also says it uses your interactions with its AI to improve AI at Meta, and that when the AI cannot answer, it shares your messages and general information such as your region with select partners. Depending on where you live, your interactions can also personalize content and ads. The page does not say how long Meta keeps data after you delete it.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/2457110494637611/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Meta AI also builds memories about you, separate from chat history. In December 2025, The Washington Post's Geoffrey A. Fowler reported that you cannot stop Meta AI from creating memories, but you can delete them one by one in Settings under Memory. He also reported that Meta offered no way to delete chats automatically on a schedule, and no setting to stop chat contents from being used to target ads.","sources":[{"name":"The Washington Post (via The Nightly): Your AI chatbot keeps a file on you","url":"https://thenightly.com.au/society/technology/the-washington-post-your-ai-chatbot-keeps-a-file-on-you-heres-how-to-delete-it-c-21096491"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Fowler's rule of thumb is a good one: do not tell a chatbot anything you would not want to see on social media. Deleting afterward helps, but not sharing it in the first place helps more.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Meta AI also runs inside Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp, and each app has its own help page for those chats, according to Meta's help center. The steps in this guide cover the Meta AI app, Vibes and meta.ai.","sources":[{"name":"Meta Help Center: Meta AI and Vibes","url":"https://www.meta.com/help/artificial-intelligence/3898022273743835/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest limit of this tool is that it controls what you can see, not everything Meta keeps. Meta's page describes what disappears from your History, Media and Create sections. It does not promise that the data is erased from Meta's systems right away, so treat deletion as cleanup, not a guarantee.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Replit Agent to build an app
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Click Plan in the chat box or type /plan. Agent splits your app into a task list before it writes code. Read it, then pick Accept tasks or Revise plan. Free Mode costs nothing within your plan's allowance. On Core and Pro it resets every five hours. Sources: Replit Docs: Agent overview, Replit Docs: Pricing and plans, Replit Docs: Agent billing, Replit Docs: Free Mode, Replit Docs: Checkpoints and rollbacks, Replit Docs: Publishing, Replit Docs: Prompting guide, All About Cookies: Replit review, DEV Community: Replit Agent review 2026.

{"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Replit Agent to build an app","dek":"How to plan, build, roll back and publish an app with Replit Agent, what the Free, Power and Max modes cost, and where the tool still falls short.","summary":"Replit Agent turns a plain language description into a working app, tests it and can publish it to a .replit.app address. Free Mode covers everyday work within a plan's allowance, while Power and Max modes are billed by effort.","seo_title":"How to use Replit Agent to build an app, step by step","seo_description":"How to use Replit Agent: plan your app, pick Free, Power or Max mode, roll back with checkpoints, publish to .replit.app and keep the bill under control.","answer_summary":"Open a Replit project, describe the app in the Agent chat, ask for a plan with Plan or /plan, accept the tasks, test the result and click Publish. Use checkpoints to roll back and set a budget in Settings before using paid modes.","tags":["Replit","Replit Agent","Vibe coding","AI app builder","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Replit Agent builds apps from a plain language description, with no coding required. If you want to know how to use Replit to make an app, the short version is: describe it, approve a plan, let Agent build and test it, then click Publish. Replit says Agent sets up the project, writes the code, checks its own work and fixes problems, and it can also make mobile apps, slides, designs and data visualizations.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent overview","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/agent/overview"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This guide walks through a first app from start to finish, then covers the part that surprises most people: what it costs. Read the billing section before you start a big project.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Replit Agent, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Write down what the app does","text":"Before you type anything into Replit, list the features and the steps a user takes. Replit's own prompting guide puts this first: outline your app's features and user flows before you prompt. Five bullet points is enough for a first version.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Describe it to Agent","text":"Open the Project Editor and describe the app in the Agent chat. You can attach files, use voice input, or connect services such as BigQuery, Slack or Notion. You can choose the type of thing to build, such as a web app or a mobile app, but Agent can also work it out from your description.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for a plan before any code","text":"Click Plan in the chat input, type /plan, or simply ask Agent to plan. In Plan mode, Agent breaks the project into an ordered task list and compares approaches before it writes code. When the list looks right, click Accept tasks. If it does not, click Revise plan and say what to change.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Let it build, then test it yourself","text":"Agent writes the code, sets up what the app needs and tests its own work as it goes. When it finishes, click through the app like a real user would. If something is wrong, describe the problem in the chat and Agent will try to fix it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Add features one at a time","text":"Replit's guide recommends building in small steps and saving progress with checkpoints after each one that works. Ask for one feature per message, check it, then move on. When you switch to an unrelated task, start a new chat so old context does not get in the way.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Publish it","text":"Click Publish in the top right of the Project Editor. The Publish your app pane lists the domain, what you are publishing, who can access the app, and the database, monitoring, security and engagement settings. Review them and click Publish. Replit suggests a .replit.app name and checks that it is free; you can connect a custom domain after publishing.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Replit recommends Autoscale, the default deployment type, for most apps. Under Adjust settings you can see the cost per machine and the cost at maximum traffic before you commit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Replit's prompting guide asks for specific prompts: name the output, the limits and the edge cases, say what you want instead of what to avoid, and use plain bullet points for complex requests. For bugs, it says to paste the exact error message, the file names, what you were trying to do and what you already tried.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Prompting guide","url":"https://docs.replit.com/getting-started/quickstarts/build-with-ai"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The first version","text":"Build a simple web app where [who] can [main task].
Features:
- [feature 1]
- [feature 2]
- [feature 3]
Store [data] in a database. Use a clean, simple design. Start with the smallest version that works, and tell me how to test it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan only","text":"/plan I want to add [feature] to this app. Compare two ways to do it, list the files you would change, and do not write any code yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a bug","text":"When I [action] on the [page name] page, I get this error: [paste the exact error]. I expected [what should happen]. I already tried [what you tried]. Find the cause and fix only that.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Checkpoints: your undo button","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent creates checkpoints on its own, for example after a feature is finished and before it fixes a serious error. A checkpoint captures the project files and packages, the AI conversation, environment and publishing settings, and database contents. To go back, open the Agent tab, find the checkpoint and select Rollback to here, then confirm.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Checkpoints and rollbacks","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/version-control/checkpoints-and-rollbacks"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two details matter. Your development database is not restored by default: select Database under Additional rollback options to include it. And a rollback never restores the production database of a published app; Replit points to a point in time restore for that. If you make new changes after rolling back, the later checkpoints become a separate branch you cannot roll forward to.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Checkpoints and rollbacks","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/version-control/checkpoints-and-rollbacks"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Replit Agent costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent has three modes. Free Mode covers everyday work at no extra cost within your plan's allowance; on Core and Pro the allowance resets every five hours and also has a weekly limit, and you can check it under Settings, then Usage. Power is a paid mid tier mode and Max a paid top tier mode with the strongest models. When a request needs more than Free Mode, Agent explains why and asks first, and after a one time paid step it returns to Free Mode.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent overview","url":"https://docs.replit.com/references/agent/overview"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Free Mode","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/free-agent-mode"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid work is priced by effort, so a small fix costs less than a whole feature. Each request produces one checkpoint, with no charges in between. Planning in Power or Max is billed like any other request, even when no code changes. You can see the cost of each checkpoint in the Agent tab by hovering over the usage icon, and a full breakdown at replit.com/usage, which can lag by up to 30 minutes.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Pricing and plans","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/pricing-and-plans"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent billing","url":"https://docs.replit.com/billing/ai-billing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Replit's help center lists three plans for individuals. Starter is free, with a daily AI allowance, limited monthly cloud credits and one published app. Core costs $204 a year on annual billing and includes $20 in monthly credits, unlimited published apps and up to 5 collaborators. Pro costs $100 a month and adds more Free Mode usage, up to 15 builders and credits that roll over for two months. Credits also pay for published apps, storage and databases.","sources":[{"name":"Replit Docs: Pricing and plans","url":"https://docs.replit.com/help/pricing-and-plans"},{"name":"Replit Docs: Agent billing","url":"https://docs.replit.com/billing/ai-billing"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Set a budget before you use Power or Max. On the Billing page in Settings you can add usage alerts at spending thresholds and budget limits that act as hard caps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Replit Agent falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Independent testers like the speed but warn about cost and depth. An All About Cookies reviewer who built a legal case management app from a 23 page spec ran through the free plan's allowance in about 21 minutes, then used up a month of Core credits and was still an estimated 10 to 15 percent from a deployable app. A DEV Community review found that Agent's self testing catches obvious bugs but lets architecture problems through, and that custom CI/CD, strict Git workflows and hosting outside Replit add friction.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: Replit review","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/replit-review"},{"name":"DEV Community: Replit Agent review 2026","url":"https://dev.to/jovan_chan_9500711396d4e6/replit-agent-review-2026-from-idea-to-deployed-app-but-read-the-credit-bill-first-4cma"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Replit Agent is good at getting a simple idea to a live link fast, especially if you do not code. It is weaker at large, complex apps, where every round of fixes costs money and the structure of the code matters. Start small, plan first, keep each request narrow, and watch the usage page. If the project grows, expect to read the code yourself or bring in someone who can.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Kling vs Seedance: which AI video model to use, and what each one costs
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Kling 4.0 makes clips of 3 to 30 seconds in one pass, with up to 10 keyframes. Its Omni Reference takes up to 15 assets: images, videos, subjects and voices. Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one request. Sources: Kling AI: Kling 3.0 credit cost guide, Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide, Kling AI: Kling 4.0, Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users, ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch, Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0, Dreamina: Seedance 2.0 Lite.

Pick Seedance 2.0 if you want to combine images, video and audio references in one request and get stereo sound generated with the picture.","tags":["Kling AI","Seedance","Dreamina","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling vs Seedance is the choice most people face once they move past the AI video tools built into the big US chatbots. Kling is the video model from the Chinese company Kuaishou, and its newest version, Kling 4.0, launched for all users on October 15, 2026 after an early access phase that began on September 30. Seedance is ByteDance's video model. Its Seed team launched Seedance 2.0 on February 12, 2026, and consumers reach it through Dreamina, ByteDance's image and video site.","sources":[{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The short answer: Kling is the better pick when you need a longer clip or precise control over where the shot goes. Seedance is the better pick when you want to throw a pile of references at the model, including a voice or a piece of music, and get the sound back with the picture.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Kling vs Seedance at a glance","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Clip length: Kling says Kling 4.0 generates natively from 3 to 30 seconds in a single pass, and that video extension forward or backward will reach up to 2 minutes in total. Kling's older VIDEO 3.0 model runs from 3 to 15 seconds. Seedance 2.0 returns up to 15 seconds of multi-shot video, according to ByteDance's launch post.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"References: Kling 4.0's Omni Reference accepts up to 15 assets combined. Kling's FAQ breaks that down as up to 10 images, up to 5 reference videos with a combined length of up to 30 seconds, and up to 7 subject elements, and it also takes voices. You can set up to 10 keyframes. Seedance 2.0 takes text plus up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips in one generation. Dreamina says each video or audio reference can be up to 15 seconds long.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Sound: Seedance 2.0 makes the audio together with the video. Kling's VIDEO 3.0 also has Native Audio, which covers dialogue, lip sync, ambience and sound effects, and its guide lists speech in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, with dialects and accents. Kling's Kling 4.0 page does not describe audio.","sources":[{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Kling AI: VIDEO 3.0 model user guide","url":"https://kling.ai/quickstart/klingai-video-3-model-user-guide"},{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 3.0 credit cost guide","url":"https://kling.ai/blog/kling-video-3-0-credit-cost-guide"},{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Picture: Kling 4.0 offers 21:9, 16:9, 1:1 and 9:16 frames. Dreamina says Seedance 2.0 videos download at 1080p.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 4.0","url":"https://kling.ai/feature/kling-4-ai-video-generation"},{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"},{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Free credits and prices","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling sells credits through monthly plans. Its credit guide, dated July 28, 2026, lists a free Basic plan with no monthly credits and output that is not for commercial use. Pro comes with 3,000 credits, Premier with 8,000 and Ultra with 26,000. Native 4K on VIDEO 3.0 costs 30 credits a second.","sources":[{"name":"Kling AI: Kling 3.0 credit cost guide","url":"https://kling.ai/blog/kling-video-3-0-credit-cost-guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kling had not announced pricing for Kling 4.0 when it launched, according to Let's Data Science, so check the credit cost shown in the app before you generate with it.","sources":[{"name":"Let's Data Science: Kling AI opens Kling 4.0 to all users","url":"https://letsdatascience.com/news/kling-ai-opens-kling-40-to-all-users-d9dc6422"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Dreamina says you can start Seedance with no credit card. It also offers a lighter model, listed as Seedance 2.0 Lite on one page and Seedance 2.0 mini in its menus, which it describes as faster and cheaper to run and free to try with trial credits. Dreamina's menus also list a newer Seedance 2.5.","sources":[{"name":"Dreamina: How to use Seedance 2.0","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/resource/how-to-use-seedance-2-0"},{"name":"Dreamina: Seedance 2.0 Lite","url":"https://dreamina.capcut.com/seedance/seedance-2-0-lite"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Neither one is truly free for regular use. If you only need a handful of clips, start on Seedance Lite; if you plan to generate every week, compare Kling's monthly credits with the cost per clip that Dreamina shows you before you pay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one to pick","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. You need a clip longer than 15 seconds","text":"Use Kling 4.0. It is the only one of the two that generates up to 30 seconds in one pass, so you avoid stitching two clips that do not quite match.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. You want to control exactly where the shot goes","text":"Use Kling 4.0 and set keyframes. Up to 10 of them let you pin the frames the video has to pass through.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. You have a voice, a song or a sound to match","text":"Use Seedance 2.0. Upload the audio clip next to your images and refer to each file in the prompt by name with an @ sign, the way Dreamina's guide shows (@AssetName).","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. You just want to try AI video today","text":"Open Dreamina and pick the Lite or mini model. It runs on trial credits, and the steps are the same as for the full model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts to test both on the same shot","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The fairest test is one prompt in both tools at the same length. Keep it to one subject, one camera move and one sound, so you can see which model handles the basics better before you spend credits on a long scene.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: One subject, one camera move","text":"A slow push-in on [subject] in [place] at [time of day], soft light from the left. At the third second, [subject] turns and looks at the camera. Quiet ambient sound of [place].","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A product from one photo","text":"[Product] sits on a wooden kitchen counter in morning light. Its launch post says the model is still far from perfect: detail stability, realism and natural motion need work, keeping several subjects consistent is hard, text inside the video is not always accurate, and the audio can occasionally distort.","sources":[{"name":"ByteDance Seed: Seedance 2.0 official launch","url":"https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/official-launch-of-seedance-2-0"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Using a real person's face as a Seedance reference requires identity verification or prior legal authorization, according to ByteDance. item.title: Amazon is close to a $7.5 billion AI deal
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Amazon is in advanced talks to buy San Francisco startup Decart at a valuation of about $7.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on November 21. A deal could come within days, though talks could still collapse. Amazon declined to comment. Decart, founded in 2023, makes software that helps AI models run more efficiently and frees up chip capacity. It was an early user of Amazon's Trainium chips, which Amazon built to compete with Nvidia's GPUs. Sources: PYMNTS, Seeking Alpha, GeekWire, The Seattle Times via The Spokesman-Review.

The API key field is required by OpenAI clients but Ollama ignores it. LM Studio also offers an OpenAI compatible API and a REST API in beta, which the Machine Learning Mastery comparison puts on port 1234.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama Docs: OpenAI compatibility","url":"https://docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility"},{"name":"LM Studio Docs","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app"},{"name":"Machine Learning Mastery: Ollama vs LM Studio vs llama.cpp","url":"https://machinelearningmastery.com/ollama-vs-lm-studio-vs-llama-cpp-which-local-ai-runtime-should-you-use-in-2026/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Model formats: LM Studio runs models with llama.cpp on all three systems and can also use Apple's MLX on Apple Silicon Macs. Machine Learning Mastery notes that Ollama picks a well tuned 4 bit version of a model by default, while LM Studio lists the available versions and shows which ones fit your memory.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio Docs","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app"},{"name":"Machine Learning Mastery: Ollama vs LM Studio vs llama.cpp","url":"https://machinelearningmastery.com/ollama-vs-lm-studio-vs-llama-cpp-which-local-ai-runtime-should-you-use-in-2026/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Check your computer before you install","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio lists clear minimums. On a Mac it needs Apple Silicon (M1 to M4) and macOS 14 or newer, and Intel Macs are not supported. On Windows it runs on x64 and ARM chips such as Snapdragon X Elite, and x64 processors need AVX2. On Linux it ships as an AppImage for x64 and ARM64 and needs Ubuntu 20.04 or newer.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio Docs: System requirements","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/system-requirements"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For memory, LM Studio recommends 16GB of RAM, and on Windows at least 4GB of dedicated graphics memory. It says 8GB Macs may work with smaller models and a modest context length.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio Docs: System requirements","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/system-requirements"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The model, not the app, decides what your computer can handle. Start with a small model, see how fast it answers, then try a bigger one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to start with each one","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. LM Studio: download and chat","text":"Install LM Studio, open it, search for a model, download it and start a chat. LM Studio also ships a command line tool called lms, but you have to open the app at least once before lms works.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"LM Studio commands to try","text":"lms ls
lms load openai/gpt-oss-20b
lms server start","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Ollama: pull a model and point your app at it","text":"Install Ollama, download a model from the terminal, then send requests to the local address from any tool that speaks the OpenAI API. Ollama's docs also show how to copy a model under an OpenAI style name so older tools work without changes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Ollama commands from its docs","text":"ollama pull llama3.2
ollama cp llama3.2 gpt-3.5-turbo","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"In Ollama you can raise the context size by creating your own model from a Modelfile with a num_ctx parameter. Bigger context needs more memory.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Price: local is free, the cloud is not","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"LM Studio has been free to use at home and at work since July 2025, with no form or separate commercial license, according to the company. Its cloud side, called Bionic, starts with a free plan for local models and limited web search, then Bionic+ at $20 a month and Pro at $100 a month, with US hosted models and zero data retention.","sources":[{"name":"LM Studio blog: Free for work","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work"},{"name":"LM Studio: Pricing","url":"https://lmstudio.ai/pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Ollama says running models on your own hardware is always unlimited. Its cloud plans start at $0 with pay per token pricing, then Pro at $20 a month with $60 of usage included, Max at $100 a month with $300 included, and Team at $500 a month. Ollama moved to per token pricing on August 31, 2026, and says prompts and answers are never logged or trained on.","sources":[{"name":"Ollama: Pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/pricing"},{"name":"Ollama blog: Transparent pricing","url":"https://ollama.com/blog/transparent-pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Which one to use","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Choose LM Studio if you are new to local AI, want to browse models visually and mostly chat or ask questions about your own files. It is the most forgiving way to see what your computer can run.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Choose Ollama if you write code, use coding agents or want a model running in the background that other apps can call. Its API is small, documented and close to OpenAI's, so many tools connect with only a changed address.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The weak spots are honest ones. LM Studio does not run on Intel Macs. Ollama's OpenAI compatibility covers only part of the OpenAI API, so features such as logprobs are missing. Nothing stops you from installing both and keeping the one you open more often.","sources":[]}]}

Update the app","text":"AI Edit is rolling out on iOS, according to the help center. If you do not see it, update the app first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Start an Edit project","text":"On the Home screen, keep Edit selected and add your media. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy for faster research","dek":"Seven copy and paste prompts built on Perplexity's own help center tips, for quick answers, comparisons, Deep Research reports and files.","summary":"Seven Perplexity prompts based on the tips in Perplexity's help center. Each one adds context, asks for one thing and names the format, and three of them use Deep Research or file creation, which depend on your plan.","seo_title":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy and paste for faster research","seo_description":"7 Perplexity prompts to copy: ask with context, compare options, run Deep Research, analyze your own file and turn the results into a spreadsheet or deck.","answer_summary":"Good Perplexity prompts state one clear goal, add a line of context, use the keywords that matter and name the format (a table, bullet points or steps). For long reports, use Deep Research from the plus (+) menu, which Perplexity includes on Pro, Max and Enterprise plans.","tags":["Perplexity","Prompts","AI search","Deep Research","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"These Perplexity prompts come from Perplexity's own help center, which lists the habits that get better answers: say what you want, give context, ask for one thing at a time and name the format. Below are seven prompts built on those tips, with [brackets] where your details go. Paste one in, fill the brackets, and you get a cited answer instead of a pile of links.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center describes a good prompt as five parts: an instruction, context, the input, keywords that matter, and the output format you want. You do not need all five every time, but most weak answers miss at least two of them. The help center gives \"Cars.\" as an example of a search that is too vague to be useful.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for everyday research","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The question with context","text":"I'm a [who you are] in [where you live]. [Your question, as one clear sentence]. Give me the answer as [a table / bullet points / a step by step guide].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This is the base pattern, and every other prompt here is a version of it. Perplexity's own example is a first-time homebuyer in the US asking which federal programs can help. The context line changes the sources it picks, and the format line saves you from reformatting the answer yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Compare two options","text":"Compare the pros and cons of [option A] vs. [option B] for [your situation]. Put the result in a table with one row per point, and note which sources disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Add the keywords that actually decide the answer. The help center's example is \"best noise-canceling headphones under $200 for commuting\": the price and the use case do more work than the word headphones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Arguments for and against","text":"Summarize the main arguments for and against [idea or decision], with supporting data. Keep each side to five points and link the source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity's help center uses a four-day work week as its example for this one. It works for anything people argue about: a policy, a purchase, a career move. Asking for a fixed number of points per side keeps the answer balanced and short enough to read.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for Deep Research","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deep Research reads many sources and writes a detailed report. According to Perplexity's help center, it is included on Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max. To start it, open the plus (+) menu in the search bar and pick Deep Research; on the web you can also type / in the search bar. Perplexity notes the menu can look different depending on the platform.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report on one question","text":"Research [topic] and [what you want it to suggest or explain], including [the detail you care about most, for example cost comparisons].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Be clear about what you want to learn before you hit enter. Perplexity's sample is \"the environmental impact of fast fashion and sustainable alternatives, including cost comparisons\". The help center contrasts it with \"Tell me about fashion\", which gives Deep Research nothing to aim at.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Narrow it down","text":"Now focus on [one part of the report]. What does the evidence say, and where is it weak?","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start broad, then narrow with follow-ups in the same thread, as the help center recommends. Its example is a report on remote work trends in the United States since 2020, followed by \"Now focus on the impact on employee productivity.\" One big question and two short follow-ups usually beat one giant prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Your file plus the web","text":"Based on the attached [report, contract or spreadsheet] and the latest [market data or news], what's the outlook for [company, product or plan]? Separate what comes from my file and what comes from the web.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center says you can upload your own files and ask Deep Research to analyze them next to web sources, using an attached financial report as its example. The last sentence of the prompt above is our addition: it makes it easier to see which claims came from your document.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts that make a file","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Turn research into a document, deck or sheet","text":"Build a spreadsheet comparing the top [5] [tools or products] by [price], [features] and [user ratings].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Depending on your plan, Perplexity can create documents, slide decks and spreadsheets, and the help center says documents include citations. Say the file type plainly, for example \"Create a Word document\", \"Build a slide deck\" or \"Make a spreadsheet\", and describe the structure, such as a 10-slide presentation with sections on budget, channels and key metrics. Documents export as .pdf or .docx, presentations as .pptx and spreadsheets as .xlsx.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Fix the file with short follow-ups instead of rewriting the prompt. The help center's examples are \"Add a conclusion slide\" and \"Make the executive summary shorter.\" You can also run a search first and then ask Perplexity to turn the results into a document or deck in the same session, if your plan includes file creation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to write your own Perplexity prompts","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start with one clear goal","text":"Write the question you would ask an expert, not a search keyword. Asking for the current inflation rate in the US works; \"inflation\" makes Perplexity guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add who you are and why you ask","text":"One sentence of background is enough. Perplexity's tips and the University of Florida Business Library's guide both point out that context and follow-up questions are what turn a generic answer into a useful one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for one thing and name the format","text":"A table, bullet points or a step by step guide. If you need three things, ask three times in the same thread.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Test and tweak","text":"Perplexity's help center tells users to test prompts and adjust them. If the answer misses, change one part of the prompt (the context, the keywords or the format), not all of it at once.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is only as good as the question. Vague prompts get vague answers, and the help center says so with examples like \"Cars.\" and \"Write something for me.\" Usage limits depend on your plan, the help center lists Deep Research only for Pro, Max and Enterprise plans, file creation also depends on the plan, and every regenerated or edited image counts as a new generation toward your image limit. The citations make it easy to check an answer, so open at least one source for any number you plan to reuse.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google is killing the Nest app and Assistant on speakers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Nest app stops working on Android, iOS and the web on January 25, 2027. The Google Home app takes over. Devices, settings and schedules move over on their own, according to 9to5Google. Google Assistant leaves compatible speakers and smart displays on August 2, 2027. Gemini for Home replaces it. Download your saved Nest clips first: they do not transfer. Sources: 9to5Google, Android Central, How-To Geek, Google Home blog.

To use it from your phone, create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and add the token with openclaw channels add.","tags":["OpenClaw","AI agents","Telegram","Open source AI","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenClaw is an open source AI assistant that runs on your own hardware and answers you in the chat apps you already use, according to its documentation. It runs a Gateway on your machine, works with many AI models, and has no paid tier. If you want to know how to use OpenClaw, the short version is: install it with one command, reuse an AI login you already have, then connect a chat app like Telegram.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Why OpenClaw","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not a toy. That is why it is useful, and why the safety section of this guide matters more than the install. The project was earlier known as ClawdBot and then Moltbot, Malwarebytes reported.","sources":[{"name":"Malwarebytes: OpenClaw, what is it and can you use it safely?","url":"https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/openclaw-what-is-it-and-can-you-use-it-safely"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs list two requirements. You need Node.js 24.16.0 or newer on the 24 line, or 26.1.0 or newer, and Node 26 is the recommended version. You also need some way to reach an AI model: an existing Claude Code or Codex CLI login, or an API key from a model provider. OpenClaw itself is free; the AI model you connect is what you may pay for.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Install","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/install"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Check your Node version first with node --version.
