Run the installer","text":"On macOS, Linux or WSL2, the docs give this command: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash. On Windows PowerShell it is iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex. The script detects your system, installs Node if needed, installs OpenClaw and starts onboarding. If you would rather just try it first, npx openclaw@latest runs it without the installer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Quick start","text":"Onboarding offers Quick start and Custom setup. Quick start looks for a Claude Code or Codex login or an API key you already have, checks that it works with a real request, saves the config and opens the web dashboard. If nothing it finds works, it switches to manual provider setup. You can change settings later with openclaw configure.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Keep it running in the background","text":"In Quick start the Gateway runs in your terminal until you press Ctrl+C. To keep it running, stop it and run openclaw gateway install. That installs a background service: a LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux and WSL2, or a Scheduled Task on Windows. Your config is kept.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check it and open the dashboard","text":"Run openclaw gateway status and you should see the Gateway listening on port 18789. Then run openclaw dashboard. It opens the Control UI in your browser, where you can type a message and get a reply from your assistant.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"On Windows, the docs recommend the native Windows Hub companion app as the easiest path. There is also a macOS menu bar app if you prefer a normal app download over the terminal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Connect OpenClaw to Telegram","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs call Telegram the fastest channel to set up, because it only needs a bot token. Other channels include Discord, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Slack and WhatsApp.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Telegram setup","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/telegram/setup"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create a bot with BotFather","text":"Open Telegram and start a chat with @BotFather. Check that the handle is exactly @BotFather. Send /newbot, follow the prompts and save the token it gives you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Give OpenClaw the token","text":"Run openclaw channels add --channel telegram --token followed by your bot token. Then run openclaw channels status --probe to confirm Telegram is ready. Telegram does not use a login command; the token is all it needs.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Approve your first message","text":"Send any message to your bot. With the default pairing policy, that message is not processed. Instead it creates a pairing request. Run openclaw pairing list telegram, then openclaw pairing approve telegram with the code shown. Codes expire after one hour.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pairing is OpenClaw's approval step for who may talk to your agent. Unknown senders get a short code and their message is ignored until you approve it. You can also approve requests in the Control UI under Settings, Channels, DM access requests. Approving a direct message does not give that person access in groups.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Pairing","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/pairing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to keep OpenClaw safe","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The OpenClaw docs say the defaults are conservative: on a normal install the Gateway only listens on your own machine, most chat channels answer unknown senders with a pairing code, and group access is allowlisted. The same docs are clear that sandboxing is off by default. They offer one command to check your setup: openclaw security audit.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Security","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Why OpenClaw","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outside researchers are more cautious. Malwarebytes reported problems including prompt injection, exposed instances and a growing ecosystem of dubious third party plugins, and noted that the Dutch data protection authority warned organizations not to run experimental agents like OpenClaw on systems with sensitive data. Its advice, based on Microsoft's recommendations, is to run such agents in a sandboxed virtual machine or container, give them their own limited accounts, and treat every new skill as new code.","sources":[{"name":"Malwarebytes: OpenClaw, what is it and can you use it safely?","url":"https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/openclaw-what-is-it-and-can-you-use-it-safely"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Do not install OpenClaw on the laptop that holds your bank, work and password manager logins. Use a spare machine, a virtual machine or a container, connect only the accounts it needs, and install skills only from sources you trust.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"If OpenClaw does not work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Run openclaw triage. The docs say it runs read only health checks and writes a cleaned up description of the problem, then offers to hand it to a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex. Secrets, tokens and raw logs are left out. To read the findings yourself, run openclaw doctor instead.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"OpenClaw is a good fit if you are comfortable in a terminal and want an assistant you control, on your own hardware, reachable from your phone. It is a poor fit if you want something that is safe with no thought: an agent that can run commands needs the same care as any program you give admin rights. Start small, with one channel, one model and no sensitive accounts, and widen access only when you trust what it does.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Signal is now blocking Siri and Gemini from reading your private chats on your own phone
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting stops screenshots inside the app, so Siri cannot read your chats off the screen. The catch: you cannot screenshot your own chats either. Settings > App Security in Signal for iOS. On supported Android phones, Signal turns on Screen security when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen. Mac users must add Signal to Excluded Apps under System Settings > Siri. Signal is asking Apple, Google and Microsoft for a clear way for apps to keep AI out of screens, files, notifications and APIs. Sources: BleepingComputer, Coywolf.

nf:hero.nf:alt: Screenshot of Signal's App Security settings on an iPhone showing the Block Siri AI option.

item.title: Trump and Xi agreed AI should never launch a major military action without a human, Bessent says
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Friday that Trump and Xi agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use AI. He called it one of the major achievements of Trump's Asia trip. Bessent said AI "should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions." In his words, no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved. Bessent said the deal does not change the race for AI supremacy, and US labs must keep their lead. Sources: Reuters (via Defense News), Reuters (via Yahoo News), Anadolu Agency (via A News).

item.title: Anthropic's stock fell almost to its IPO price on day two
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic priced its shares at $83. They opened on Nasdaq at $111.50 on November 19, a 34% jump. By the close they had slipped to $97.17. On November 20 the stock fell as low as $83.15, just 15 cents above the IPO price. That was about 25% below its first-day high of $115.10. The slide came as tech shares fell broadly. Fortune pointed to worries about Nvidia and the midterm election results. Anthropic raised about $91 billion in its share sale. Sources: Fortune (via Yahoo Finance), Decrypt, Futurism.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Code prompts: 8 to copy and paste for real projects","dek":"Eight prompts built on Anthropic's own Claude Code advice, for understanding a codebase, fixing bugs, building features and reviewing changes.","summary":"Eight copy and paste Claude Code prompts based on the patterns in Anthropic's documentation. Most of them give Claude a way to verify its work, such as a failing test or a build that has to pass.","seo_title":"Claude Code prompts: 8 to copy and paste for real projects","seo_description":"8 Claude Code prompts to copy and paste: explore a codebase, plan in plan mode, fix bugs with a failing test, write tests and review changes with a subagent.","answer_summary":"The best Claude Code prompts are specific and include a way to check the result: name the files, describe the symptom, and ask for a failing test or a passing build. Plan larger changes in plan mode (Shift+Tab) first, and use /clear between tasks.","tags":["Claude Code","Claude","Prompts","AI coding","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"These Claude Code prompts come from the patterns Anthropic recommends in its own Claude Code documentation, rewritten with [brackets] so you can paste them into your own project. The short version: give Claude a way to check its work, plan before it codes, and be specific about files and the result you want. Vague prompts get vague code.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Common workflows","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's best practices page makes one point above the rest: Claude does better when it can verify its own work, with a test to run, a build that has to pass, or a screenshot to compare against. Most prompts below build that check into the request.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Claude Code prompts for understanding a codebase","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Get the lay of the land","text":"Give me an overview of this codebase. Explain the main architecture patterns and the key data models, then tell me which files handle [feature].","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You can point at files directly with @, for example @src/utils/auth.js. Typing @ opens a menu of paths, and Anthropic's docs note it also loads the CLAUDE.md files from that folder and its parents.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan before code","text":"I want to add [feature]. Read [folder] first. What files need to change? Create a plan before writing any code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"How to turn on plan mode","text":"Press Shift+Tab until the status bar shows that plan mode is on, or start a session with claude --permission-mode plan. In plan mode Claude reads and proposes but does not edit. Press Ctrl+G to edit the plan in your own editor, then approve it or press Shift+Tab to leave. Anthropic says to skip planning for changes you could describe in one sentence, because it adds overhead.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for fixing bugs","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a bug the right way","text":"Users report that [what goes wrong]. Check [folder]. Write a failing test that reproduces the issue, then fix it and run the tests again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The failing test is the important part. It proves the bug exists, and when it passes you know the fix did something. Without it you are trusting Claude's word.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Fix the build, not the symptom","text":"The build fails with this error: [paste error]. Fix it and confirm the build passes. Fix the root cause, do not suppress the error.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for building features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Copy your own patterns","text":"Look at how [existing component] is built to understand our patterns. Follow the same pattern to build [new component]. Use only libraries already in this codebase.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Let it interview you","text":"I want to build [short description]. Interview me in detail about the implementation, UI, edge cases and tradeoffs. Skip obvious questions. When we are done, write a full spec to SPEC.md.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Anthropic suggests building from the finished spec in a fresh session, so the long interview does not fill the context Claude needs for the code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for tests and review","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Fill the test gaps","text":"Find the functions in [file] that are not covered by tests. Add tests for them, including edge cases, then run the new tests and fix any failures.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Get a second opinion","text":"Use a subagent to review the changes against [PLAN.md]. Check that every requirement is implemented and the edge cases have tests. Report gaps, not style preferences.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A subagent works in its own context, so the review is not shaped by the session that wrote the code. Anthropic's docs warn that reviewers tend to over-report, which is why the prompt asks for gaps and not style. When you are happy, a plain request to commit with a descriptive message and open a pull request finishes the job.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Common workflows","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Setup that makes every prompt work better","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Run /init","text":"The /init command writes a starter CLAUDE.md, a file Claude reads at the start of every session. Keep it short: the test commands, the stack, and rules Claude keeps getting wrong. Anthropic's test for each line is whether removing it would cause mistakes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Use /clear between tasks","text":"Performance drops as the context window fills, and Claude can start forgetting earlier instructions. Clear the session when you switch tasks, and if you have corrected Claude twice on the same thing, Anthropic suggests clearing and starting over with a better prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Name your stack","text":"SitePoint's guide to Claude Code workflows recommends writing the exact versions of your frameworks into CLAUDE.md, because without them Claude may invent imports or use the wrong version of an API. It also warns against putting secrets in CLAUDE.md, since the file is usually committed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Claude Code still struggles","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Long sessions are the weak spot. Anthropic's docs say a single debugging session can use tens of thousands of tokens, a bloated CLAUDE.md makes Claude ignore instructions, and checkpoints only track edits made through Claude's file tools, so they are no substitute for git. SitePoint suggests starting a new session after three or four chained steps.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Anthropic Engineering: Claude Code best practices","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-best-practices"},{"name":"SitePoint: Claude Code workflows","url":"https://www.sitepoint.com/claude-code-workflows-a-practical-pattern-guide/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Small, specific tasks with a clear check at the end beat one giant prompt. If a prompt has no way for Claude to prove it worked, add one.","sources":[]}]}

Deep analyzes 50 papers and writes a full report with diagrams and tables, meant for thesis work.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: a comparison table in Pro mode","text":"Create a table comparing the effectiveness of [approach A], [approach B] and [approach C] for [problem], with the study type and sample size for each finding.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to narrow and check the results","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Add filters","text":"Open the filter button next to Export. The filters in Consensus's guide are Journal Rank, Countries, Publish Year, Methodology, Sample Size, Study Durations, Fields of Study and Citations. You can set them before or after a search. SMU's library found that filtering for a discipline works well, while asking for a discipline in the question does not.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Use Boolean search for precise results","text":"Consensus supports AND, OR and NOT in capital letters, quotes for exact phrases and parentheses for grouping. Its guide gives this example: therapy AND (PTSD OR trauma) AND veterans. For medical topics, it suggests using MeSH terms.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Cite and export","text":"The quotation mark button creates a citation in APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, BibTeX or AMA. The download button exports results as RIS or CSV, and Consensus lists Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley, RefWorks, Citavi and Papers as supported reference managers. A link marked PDF is open access, while Full Text means the paper is behind a paywall.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Look for the checkmark next to a citation. Consensus's guide says a checkmark means the full text was analyzed. No checkmark means the summary came from the abstract only.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Consensus is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Consensus is open about its limits. Its own guide warns that AI can miss nuances, limitations or caveats, that not all studies are equally rigorous, and that you should never copy its summaries into a paper or cite a paper whose abstract you have not read. Oregon State notes it does not search subscription databases such as Web of Science, and SMU says it does not cover scholarly books.","sources":[{"name":"Consensus LibGuide for Academic Research","url":"https://consensus.app/home/resources/consensus-libguide-for-academic-research/"},{"name":"Oregon State University Libraries: Consensus","url":"https://guides.library.oregonstate.edu/consensus"},{"name":"SMU Libraries: Get the most out of Consensus","url":"https://blog.smu.edu/smulibraries/2025/10/03/get-the-most-out-of-consensus-an-ai-academic-search-tool"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SMU Libraries puts it plainly: use Consensus as a discovery tool, not a decision making tool. Not every result will be relevant, and people doing formal systematic reviews are warned that using a language model can cause methodological problems.","sources":[{"name":"SMU Libraries: Get the most out of Consensus","url":"https://blog.smu.edu/smulibraries/2025/10/03/get-the-most-out-of-consensus-an-ai-academic-search-tool"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The practical way to use it: ask a clear question, read the meter as a rough signal, then open the strongest papers yourself. Consensus is fast at finding studies and showing which way they point. It is not a replacement for reading them.","sources":[]}]}

Either Anthropic has a real outage, Claude is briefly out of capacity, you have hit a usage or length limit, or your login is failing on your side. Anthropic's help center has a page called Troubleshoot Claude error messages that covers each case, and the fix is different for every one. So the first job is to work out which one you are looking at.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Troubleshoot Claude error messages","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12466728-troubleshoot-claude-error-messages"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Step one: check if Claude is down","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. If you see an active incident for claude.ai, the apps or Claude Code, there is nothing to fix on your end. You can subscribe to an incident there to get updates by email or text.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outages do happen, and they tend to hit everything at once. On September 29, 2026, Anthropic's status page reported elevated errors on claude.ai, the desktop and mobile apps, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API. The problems started at 14:00 UTC and services were back to normal at 14:59 UTC. During that hour, a second issue also blocked many sign ins, new chats, file uploads and purchases.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Status","url":"https://status.claude.com/incidents/4xvtc2gnq73l"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"During that incident Anthropic asked users who were already signed in not to sign out, and said retrying might work. That is good advice for any outage: logging out and back in can leave you locked out until sign in is fixed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Earlier in the year, on January 22, 2026, TechRadar tracked another outage in which users saw a message asking them to try again, on both desktop and mobile, while Claude Code had a separate sign in problem. Reports on Downdetector rose above 2,000 before Anthropic marked the issue resolved later that morning. TechRadar pointed readers to the status page for official updates.","sources":[{"name":"TechRadar","url":"https://www.techradar.com/news/live/claude-anthropic-january-22-2026-outage"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Claude not working but there is no outage","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. A capacity error: wait a few minutes","text":"If you see \"Due to unexpected capacity constraints, Claude is unable to respond to your message. Please try again soon,\" Claude is busy, not broken. Anthropic says these are not outages, they do not appear on the status page and they usually clear up within a few minutes. Wait, then send the message again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. A usage limit: check when it resets","text":"Paid plans have a weekly limit, and most also have a five hour session limit. When you get close, Claude shows \"Approaching session limit\" or \"Approaching weekly limit.\" When you hit it, the message tells you when it resets, for example \"5-hour limit reached\" with a time. If you have turned on usage credits in your usage settings, Claude keeps going and bills those credits instead of stopping, until you reach your monthly spend limit or the balance runs out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. A length limit: split the work","text":"\"Your message will exceed the length limit for this chat\" means the conversation plus your files is too big. Anthropic suggests attaching fewer or smaller files, splitting long content into chunks, asking Claude to find the relevant part first, or starting a new conversation. On paid plans with code execution turned on, long chats are summarized automatically.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. A login error: clean up your browser","text":"For errors like \"There was an error logging you in,\" Anthropic lists three steps in order: do not use a VPN, disable browser extensions, and clear your browser cache and cookies. If none of that works, go back to status.claude.com and look for an incident affecting sign in.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"When Claude works but the answers are wrong","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Sometimes Claude runs fine but gives answers that are wrong. Anthropic calls this hallucinating and says Claude should not be your only source of truth, especially for high stakes advice. When Claude uses web search, check the sources it cites, since the original page may have context the answer leaves out. You can report a bad answer with the thumbs down button.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Incorrect or misleading responses","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A related problem is Claude claiming it did something it cannot do. Anthropic's help center says Claude can make up links that do not work, or say it sent an email or created a document, when it has no tool connected for that. If you did not connect email or a file tool, nothing was sent.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Help Center: Links that don't work and false claims","url":"https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Read the exact wording of the error before you try anything. \"Capacity constraints,\" \"limit reached\" and \"error logging you in\" each point to a different fix, and only a real outage shows up on the status page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The quick order to follow: status page first, then the message on screen, then your browser. Most of the time the answer is either a short wait or a limit that resets on a schedule. Clearing cookies or reinstalling the app will not help with either, so save those steps for login errors.","sources":[]}]}

Change the model before you send the request, not after.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is the fix for a common complaint: you upload two photos, ask Gemini to combine them, and the result ignores one of them. Install the desktop app","text":"Download Granola from its website. On a Mac, open the downloaded file and drag Granola into your Applications folder. On Windows, run the installer. The Mac app needs macOS 14 or later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in with Google or Microsoft","text":"Click Sign in and finish in your browser. Granola only supports Google and Microsoft sign-in. Use your work account if you have one, because Granola builds your meeting list from that calendar. When it asks for calendar permissions, choose Select all, then Continue.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Allow audio access","text":"On a Mac, click Allow on the microphone and system audio prompts. Windows grants both automatically. Watch the demo meeting","text":"After the first sign-in, Granola opens a short demo meeting that shows the whole flow in about two minutes. Start a note when the call starts","text":"Click the meeting notification, open the meeting from your home screen, or click New Note for a call that is not on your calendar. Templates only work in the desktop apps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Make your own template for each meeting you repeat, such as a weekly team check-in or a sales call. Granola's own guidance says participants should know when you use an AI notetaker, that recording laws differ by region, and that you should check with your legal or IT team. It also suggests pausing the transcript if a conversation turns sensitive.","sources":[{"name":"Granola Docs: When to use AI notetaking","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/consent-security-privacy/getting-consent"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Turn on the transparency features","text":"Go to Settings, then Preferences, then Transparency. The automated chat message posts a short notice in the meeting chat when you start transcribing. For Google Meet it needs the Granola browser extension. The Granola Watermark puts a small badge on your camera video while Granola is listening.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Granola is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Granola does not save audio or video, so there is nothing to play back when a line in the transcript looks wrong, and it cannot import recordings you already have. On desktop it captures all system audio at once, so music or other sounds on your computer can end up in the transcript. Speakers are often inferred from context, so names can be attributed to the wrong person. The phone apps cannot capture audio from video call apps.","sources":[{"name":"Granola Docs: Transcription","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/taking-notes/transcription"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Independent reviewers point to the same gaps. A review on the blog of tl;dv, a competitor, called the missing playback a real problem when a transcript in Russian came out poorly. Zack Proser, who uses Granola daily and links to it as an affiliate, recommends checking names, numbers and dates against the transcript for a few minutes after each meeting.","sources":[{"name":"tl;dv: Granola review","url":"https://tldv.io/blog/granola-review/"},{"name":"Zack Proser: Granola AI review","url":"https://zackproser.com/blog/granola-ai-review"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Granola fits people who sit in a lot of video calls, want to stay in the conversation instead of typing, and do not need a recording afterward. It fits less well if you need audio to prove what was said, or if your team has strict rules about where meeting data is processed. Try it on a few ordinary meetings on the free plan, turn on the chat message from day one, and read the first summaries closely before you trust them.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to delete all your ChatGPT chats, and what it remembers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the sidebar, hover over the chat, click the three dots and choose Delete. Confirm it. Pick Archive instead to hide it without deleting. Open Settings, then Data controls. Next to Delete all chats, click Delete all and confirm. It also clears chats inside your projects. Deleting chats does not erase all memories. Open Personalization to manage them or turn off Enable memory. Sources: OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT, All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats, and clear what ChatGPT remembers about you","dek":"Deleting one chat, deleting everything, archiving instead, and the separate memory settings most people forget. Plus what happens to your data after you hit delete.","summary":"To delete all ChatGPT chats, open Settings, go to Data controls and choose Delete all next to Delete all chats, then confirm. Deleting chats does not erase every saved memory, so memories have to be managed separately under Personalization.","seo_title":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats (and your memory)","seo_description":"Steps to delete one ChatGPT chat or all of them, archive instead, clear saved memories, stop training on your chats, and the 30 day deletion rule explained.","answer_summary":"Open ChatGPT Settings, choose Data controls, click Delete all next to Delete all chats and confirm. This removes every conversation, including chats in projects, but not all saved memories, which you manage under Personalization.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","Privacy","Chat history","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"You can delete all ChatGPT chats at once from Settings, under Data controls. One button clears your whole history, including conversations inside projects, according to OpenAI's help center. Deleted chats disappear from your sidebar right away and are permanently removed from OpenAI's systems within 30 days, unless a legal or security exception applies.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The part most people miss: deleting chats does not wipe what ChatGPT has learned about you. ChatGPT builds memories from your chat history, files and connected apps, and deleting a chat may remove a specific memory but not all of them. Memory has its own settings, covered further down.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Deleted chats cannot be brought back. OpenAI says they cannot be recovered through the app, the API or support. If there is anything you want to keep, export your data first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you delete: export your ChatGPT data","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Request a data export","text":"OpenAI's help center points to Settings, then Data controls, to request a data export. It is also a quick way to see which chats are still stored on your account before you clear them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats at once","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Settings","text":"On the web, click your profile and choose Settings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Go to Data controls","text":"Choose Data controls in the left menu of the Settings window.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Click Delete all","text":"Find Delete all chats and click Delete all next to it. Then click Confirm deletion. Every conversation goes, including the ones saved inside projects.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The same Data controls page has Archive all chats, with an Archive all button and a Confirm archive step. Archiving is not deleting: it moves chats out of the sidebar, and they stay on your account under the normal retention rules.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"},{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to delete or archive a single chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Hover over the chat in the sidebar","text":"Move your pointer over the conversation in your chat history and click the three dots next to its title.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Choose Delete or Archive","text":"Select Delete and confirm when ChatGPT asks. Select Archive instead if you only want it out of sight. Archiving needs no confirmation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Find archived chats later","text":"Open Settings, then Data controls, and click Manage next to Archived Chats. From there you can unarchive a chat, which puts it back in your history, or delete it for good.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a chat seems to have vanished, check Archived Chats before you assume it was deleted. OpenAI's help center lists that as the first thing to check.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to clear ChatGPT memory","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Manage saved memories","text":"Open Personalization from your profile menu. Under Memory summary, select Manage to see what ChatGPT has stored, then update or delete individual memories.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Turn memory off","text":"In the same Personalization settings, switch off Enable memory. This stops ChatGPT from creating new memories. It does not remove the ones already saved, so delete those first if you want a clean slate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Images, training and Temporary Chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Images can outlive the chat they came from. Deleting a chat generally removes its images, but some may still sit in your Library. To remove them, open Library in the left menu, go to Images, select the pictures with the circle in the bottom right corner of each one, and click Delete.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Clearing your history does not change whether future chats are used to train OpenAI's models. That is a separate switch: in Settings, under Data controls, turn off Improve the model for everyone. It is on by default.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For conversations you never want saved, use Temporary Chat. These chats do not appear in your history, do not create new memories and are not used to improve OpenAI's models. OpenAI's deletion window of 30 days covers them too.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What happens after you delete","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chats are removed from view immediately and permanently deleted from OpenAI's systems within 30 days. OpenAI names two exceptions: a chat that was already de-identified and disconnected from your account, and a chat OpenAI must keep for security or legal reasons. Deleting a conversation also removes synced data from connected apps that was kept in it, while disconnecting an app only stops future access.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The legal exception is not theoretical. All About Cookies notes that a federal court order in a copyright lawsuit brought by publishers including The New York Times required OpenAI to produce about 20 million conversations, with personal details removed or masked.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Deleting your whole ChatGPT account","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"10. Delete the account (optional)","text":"Open Settings, choose Account, and click Delete under Delete account. Enter your account email, type DELETE and click Permanently delete my account. You cannot sign up again with the same email or phone number for 30 days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Deleting your account does not cancel a subscription you bought through the App Store or Google Play. Cancel it there first. All About Cookies also suggests deleting chats and images before deleting the account, since OpenAI does not spell out that account deletion removes them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest summary: Delete all chats is fast and thorough for your history, but it is only one of three switches. If you want ChatGPT to forget you, clear your memories under Personalization, and if you want future chats kept out of training, turn off Improve the model for everyone. These steps are written for the web version; menu names may look slightly different in the apps.","sources":[]}]}

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in at manus.im and choose a mode at the top of the task: Manus 2.0 Max for complex work, Manus 2.0 for most tasks, Lite for small edits. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Manus: your first task, the modes, and how credits work","dek":"Manus is an AI agent that does the work on its own cloud computer. Here is how to start a task, pick a mode, and keep the credit bill under control.","summary":"Manus runs tasks in a virtual computer with a browser and file system, and every task is paid for in credits that depend on how complex it is. Manus cannot estimate a task's cost in advance, so clear, specific, smaller tasks are the main way to save credits.","seo_title":"How to use Manus (and how Manus credits work)","seo_description":"How to use Manus AI: sign in, pick a mode, write a task that works, and understand how credits are spent, refreshed and refunded, with tips to use fewer.","answer_summary":"Sign in at manus.im, choose a mode such as Manus 2.0 or Manus 2.0 Lite, and describe the goal, scope and output format. Manus plans and runs the steps on its own cloud computer, and each task uses credits based on its complexity.","tags":["Manus","AI agents","Manus credits","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Manus is an AI agent: you give it a goal, and it plans the steps and carries them out in a virtual computer with internet access and a file system. The finished work, such as a report, a slide deck or a website, shows up in the task. You can use it on the web at manus.im, in the Manus Studio desktop app for macOS and Windows, in a mobile app, or by sending a task by email, according to the Manus documentation. Manus joined Meta in late 2025 and still runs its own subscription product, according to a review by Work Management.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Docs: Getting started","url":"https://manus.im/docs/introduction/quickstart"},{"name":"Work Management: Manus review","url":"https://work-management.org/website/manus-review/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The part that confuses most new users is the bill. Every task uses credits, the amount depends on how complex the task is, and Manus says it cannot tell you the cost before you start. This guide covers how to run a first task and how to keep credit use down.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Help: What are credits?","url":"https://manus.im/help/credits"},{"name":"Manus Help Center: Checking credit cost before a task","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/13185575-is-there-a-way-to-check-how-many-credits-a-task-will-cost-before-i-begin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Manus: your first task","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign in","text":"Go to manus.im and sign in. If you want Manus to work with files and apps on your own computer, download Manus Studio from manus.im/desktop and sign in with the same account. Web tasks run in Manus Cloud.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose a mode","text":"At the top of the task, pick a mode. Manus 2.0 Max is for complex tasks, Manus 2.0 is for most tasks, and Manus 2.0 Lite is for everyday tasks and small edits. Manus Flex uses your own model API key instead.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Describe the goal","text":"Write the task in plain language and include three things: the topic, the scope and the output format. \"Research X\" is vague. \"Compare five options on price and features in one table\" tells Manus when it is done.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A research task with a clear output","text":"Research the 5 most popular project management apps for small teams. Compare price, free plan limits and integrations in one table. Then make a 3 slide deck with your recommendation and the reasons for it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Let it work, then refine","text":"Manus plans the steps and runs them. When it is done, send a follow-up message in the same task to change the result. If you want to try a different direction without losing the original, create a branch from any Manus reply.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: A small website","text":"Build a one page website for [name of event] on [date] at [place]. Include a short description, a schedule with [number] items, and a simple RSVP section. Keep the design plain and readable on a phone.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use Projects for work you repeat. A project stores shared instructions and files, and every new task in it starts with that context. Click the + next to Projects in the sidebar to make one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Manus can also read from and act in other apps through Connectors, such as Gmail or Notion. Connect your account under Connectors, then mention the app in your prompt. Automations run tasks on a schedule or when something happens in a connected app.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Docs: Getting started","url":"https://manus.im/docs/introduction/quickstart"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How Manus credits work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Credits are Manus's unit of usage. They pay for the language model's tokens, the virtual machine that handles files, browsing and code, and any third-party data services a task calls. Credits are only used while a task is actively running; finished tasks and the files or sites they produced cost nothing to keep. Manus gives examples: a sports scoring chart that took 15 minutes used 200 credits, a wedding invitation page that took 25 minutes used 360, and a complex web app that took 80 minutes used 900.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Help: What are credits?","url":"https://manus.im/help/credits"},{"name":"Manus Help Center: Rules for credits consumption","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11711097-what-are-the-rules-for-credits-consumption-and-how-can-i-obtain-them"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The plans are Free, Pro and Team. Monthly plan credits refresh on the same date each month, based on when your subscription started, and unused monthly credits do not roll over. The help center gives the example of a $20 Pro membership started on January 1 that receives 4,000 monthly credits to use before February 1. Free users get daily refresh credits that work only with Manus 2.0 Lite, with a monthly cap of 1,500 daily credits.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Help Center: Rules for credits consumption","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11711097-what-are-the-rules-for-credits-consumption-and-how-can-i-obtain-them"},{"name":"Manus Docs: Plans","url":"https://manus.im/docs/introduction/plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Manus spends credits in a fixed order: event credits first, then daily, monthly, add-on and free credits. Free credits never expire. Add-on credits can be bought at any time but only work with an active paid subscription. If a task fails because of a technical problem on Manus's side, the credits it used are refunded in full.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Help: What are credits?","url":"https://manus.im/help/credits"},{"name":"Manus Help Center: Rules for credits consumption","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11711097-what-are-the-rules-for-credits-consumption-and-how-can-i-obtain-them"},{"name":"Manus Docs: Plans","url":"https://manus.im/docs/introduction/plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two details are worth knowing. A balance can briefly go negative, because each action is charged at the start of the next one, and you cannot start new tasks until it is back above zero. And Manus cannot estimate a task's cost before it begins: the help center says that if Manus quotes a credit figure in a conversation, treat it as a hallucination, not a promise.","sources":[{"name":"Manus Help Center: Rules for credits consumption","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/11711097-what-are-the-rules-for-credits-consumption-and-how-can-i-obtain-them"},{"name":"Manus Help Center: Checking credit cost before a task","url":"https://help.manus.im/en/articles/13185575-is-there-a-way-to-check-how-many-credits-a-task-will-cost-before-i-begin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use fewer credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Split big jobs into smaller tasks. Long conversations carry more context, and that raises the cost of every step.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Be precise in the first message. Clear requirements cut down on clarifying questions, and each round of back and forth uses credits. Combine related requests in one task instead of several.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Check the intermediate results on long, multi-step tasks, so you can stop a task that is heading the wrong way before it burns through more credits.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Manus is good at work with many steps that would take you an afternoon: research across many sources, a slide deck, a simple site. It is weaker when you need a predictable price, because you only learn the cost afterward, and independent testers have reported failed workflows, so important results still need a human check. Start with one small, specific task on a free account and look at how many credits it used before giving it anything big.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Topaz Video AI to upscale old video to 4K
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Drag a clip in, or use File, then Import. Then start from scratch or from a preset. Presets are saved setups you can reuse and mark as favorites. Under Enhancement, choose the Output Resolution and the Video Type. Topaz recommends the Proteus model for your first video. Render Preview renders 2 seconds by default, up to 30, so you can judge the result fast. Start with Proteus, preview a few seconds, and only reach for heavier models when the preview shows a real gain.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to cancel Perplexity, and the 24 hour refund window

item.title: How to cancel ChatGPT Plus or Pro, and keep your chats
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On chatgpt.com, open the account menu, choose Settings, then Billing. Under Cancel plan, select Cancel. Paid features stay on until the period you paid for ends. Paid in the iPhone app? Open iPhone Settings, tap your name, then Subscriptions, ChatGPT and Cancel Subscription. Deleting the app does not cancel anything. Open the Play Store, go to Subscriptions, pick ChatGPT and tap Cancel subscription. Sign in with the same Google account that paid for it. Sources: OpenAI Help Center: How do I cancel my ChatGPT subscription?, Engadget: How to cancel your ChatGPT subscription.
